_units.kc: crop coefficient: seasonal water demand = kc x reference evapotranspiration (no units)
_units.ky: yield response factor: fractional yield loss per fractional water shortfall (no units)
_units.root_depth_m: depth of soil the crop can draw water from, m
_units.n_effect: fractional change in the NEXT crop's yield (0.125 = +12.5%)
_units.carbon_effect: t C / ha / year added to the soil, relative to annual cropping
_units.base_yield: tonnes of feed per hectare in an average Nova Scotia year, relative to corn silage (= 1.0)
_units.repeat_penalty: fraction of yield lost when the crop follows itself (pest and disease carry-over)

_references.FAO-56: Allen, Pereira, Raes, Smith (1998). Crop evapotranspiration. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm
_references.OMAFRA-811: Ontario Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (2022). Agronomy Guide for Field Crops, Publication 811, Chapter 3 Forages. https://ontario.ca/files/2022-10/omafra-agronomy-guide-for-field-crops-chapter-3-en-2022-10-13.pdf
_references.OMAFRA-811-8: Ontario Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (2022). Agronomy Guide for Field Crops, Publication 811, Chapter 8 Managing for Healthy Soils, Tables 8-1 and 8-2 (D. Hooker, University of Guelph, Ridgetown Campus). https://www.ontario.ca/files/2022-10/omafra-agronomy-guide-for-field-crops-chapter-8-en-2022-10-13.pdf
_references.VandenBygaart-2010: VandenBygaart et al. (2010). Soil organic carbon stocks on long-term agroecosystem experiments in Canada. Can. J. Soil Sci. 90: 543-550. doi:10.4141/CJSS10028
_references.Poeplau-Don-2015: Poeplau and Don (2015). Carbon sequestration in agricultural soils via cultivation of cover crops: a meta-analysis. Agriculture, Ecosystems and Environment 200: 33-41.
_references.StatCan: Statistics Canada. Table 32-10-0359-01, Estimated areas, yield, production of principal field crops. Nova Scotia, average yield (kg/ha), mean of 2015-2024. Fetched 2026-11-14.

_base_yield_method: Statistics Canada Nova Scotia yields, mean of 2015-2024: corn for silage 34,628 kg/ha fresh, tame hay 4,777, barley 3,168, soybeans 3,119. Corn silage is converted to dry matter at 32.5% (Perennia-Corn: harvested at 30 to 35% whole plant dry matter), giving 11,254 kg/ha. Hay and grain are used as reported (roughly air dry). Each crop is divided by the corn silage figure.

source.kc: FAO-56 Table 12, Maize field (grain), Kc mid. Silage maize is not listed, so grain maize is used.
source.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, Maize field: 1.0-1.7 m. Lower bound used.
source.n_effect: No sourced value. Assumed 0 (no effect on the next crop).
source.carbon_effect: VandenBygaart-2010: annual cropping is the baseline, so 0.
source.base_yield: StatCan corn for silage, 34,628 kg/ha fresh x 32.5% dry matter (Perennia-Corn) = 11,254 kg/ha. This is the reference, so 1.0.
source.repeat_penalty: OMAFRA-811-8 Table 8-2 (Ridgetown, Ontario, 2010-2014, across tillage): continuous corn 8.91 t/ha against 9.63 t/ha for corn after soybean, 7.5% lower. Measured for grain corn; applied here to silage corn.

source.kc: FAO-56 Table 12, Alfalfa hay, averaged cutting effects, Kc mid.
source.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, Alfalfa hay: 1.0-2.0 m. Lower bound used.
source.n_effect: OMAFRA-811 Chapter 3: 10%-15% yield benefit to corn following alfalfa. Midpoint used. Measured for corn; applied here to any annual crop that follows.
source.carbon_effect: VandenBygaart-2010: perennial cropping stored 0.6 Mg C/ha/yr more than annual cropping (0-30 cm, seven Canadian long-term sites). Value taken from the abstract.
source.base_yield: StatCan tame hay, 4,777 kg/ha / 11,254 = 0.42. StatCan does not split hay into alfalfa and grass, so both use this value.
source.repeat_penalty: Perennial: staying in place is how it is grown, so no penalty.

source.kc: FAO-56 Table 12, Rye grass hay, averaged cutting effects, Kc mid. Used as a stand-in for mixed grass forage.
source.ky: UNVERIFIED. FAO-56 Table 24 has no grass entry; the alfalfa value is borrowed.
source.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, Grazing pasture: 0.5-1.5 m. Lower bound used.
source.n_effect: No sourced value. Assumed 0 (no effect on the next crop).
source.carbon_effect: VandenBygaart-2010: perennial cropping stored 0.6 Mg C/ha/yr more than annual cropping. Value taken from the abstract.
source.base_yield: StatCan tame hay, 4,777 kg/ha / 11,254 = 0.42. StatCan does not split hay into alfalfa and grass, so both use this value.
source.repeat_penalty: Perennial: staying in place is how it is grown, so no penalty.

source.ky: FAO-56 Table 24, Spring wheat. Barley is not listed, so spring wheat is used.
source.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, Barley: 1.0-1.5 m. Lower bound used.
source.n_effect: No sourced value. Assumed 0 (no effect on the next crop).
source.carbon_effect: VandenBygaart-2010: annual cropping is the baseline, so 0.
source.base_yield: StatCan barley, 3,168 kg/ha / 11,254 = 0.28. Grain only; straw is not counted.

source.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, Soybeans: 0.6-1.3 m. Lower bound used.
source.n_effect: No sourced value. Assumed 0 (no effect on the next crop).
source.carbon_effect: VandenBygaart-2010: annual cropping is the baseline, so 0.
source.repeat_penalty: OMAFRA-811-8 Table 8-1: continuous soybean 3.90 t/ha against 4.01 t/ha in a corn-soybean rotation. The table notes differences under 0.27 t/ha are not statistically significant, so 0 is used.

cover_crop.name: Winter cover crop (planted after each annual crop)

source.n_effect: No sourced value. Assumed 0 (no effect on the next crop).
source.carbon_effect: Poeplau-Don-2015: cover crops add about 0.32 Mg C/ha/yr (global meta-analysis). Value confirmed from a co-author's summary, not the paper itself.
